This study is focused on the comparative analysis of two enterprise grade routers, namely the Mikrotik CCR1009-8G-1S-1S+ and the FortiGate 60C. Their efficiency in terms of data transfer rate versus power consumption is evaluated on different traffic types. Two scenarios are considered: the handling of IPSec UDP traffic and the handling of both TCP and UDP.

articleTitle: Development of software for optimizing the fertilization of agricultural crop
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: The paper presents the development of software for optimizing the fertilization of agricultural crops. For some basic agricultural crops (wheat, corn, sunflower, etc.) the optimization software will be realized and algorithms and databases will be created together with an associated management system. The basic elements of the software development will be the algorithm, the database, and implicitly the information regarding the soil properties, estimated yields, environmental conditions, agrotechnical prescriptions, etc. The development of the software will allow the evaluation and simulation of the efficient use of agricultural fertilizers. Also, a decision support system will be set up for agricultural farmers to maximize agricultural production depending on the land plots allocated to a crop. The method used can be generalized for crops that have a similar calculation mode. The same principle applies to every culture; only the amount of nutrients administered is different. The proposed methodology aims to apply fertilizers on precise areas and in quantities necessary for optimal crop development. The stages of application of the methodology include both the phase before the establishment of the crop and the phase of its development until the harvest. Based on soil properties determined with high resolution using new technologies for scanning soil properties (drones, satellites, mobile scanners on the ground, multispectral sensors for vegetation crops) and based on agro-technical information, the nutrient requirement with a very high resolution is established: of the order of square meters or tens of square meters for each crop. In this way, the fertilizers will be used efficiently and will contribute to maximizing the agricultural production, reducing the consumption of fertilizers, and implicitly reducing the harmful effects on the environment.

articleTitle: Hardware and software solution for measure the vertical jump in the basketball game
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: Sport is a social phenomenon with an explosive development in recent years. With this development also increased the value of professional athletes involved in this phenomenon. More than ever, in an attempt to keep up with the new requirements, coaches aim to improve athletes' performance by improving physical and mental qualities. Often monitoring the deadly performance of athletes is a big barge. The aims of present paper are to present a device to be used in measuring the vertical jump of basketball players.

articleTitle: Design Space Exploration Scheme for Mapping Convolutional Neural Network on Zynq Zedboard
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is an important machine learning algorithm. Due to its broad applications and classification accuracy it has become hot topic in recent times. CNNs are both computationally expensive and have extensive memory accesses which has rendered it inefficient on general purpose computers. GPU implementations have improved the performance of algorithm but high energy consumption of GPUs doesn't allow its usage in robotics and mobile embedded platforms. In this paper we study the mapping of Convolutional Neural Networks on field programmable gate arrays (FPGAs). We implement a VGG-16 style network which are the most admired CNN architectures in community. We Used Xilinx Zynq Zedboard for analytical modeling and mapping of CNN. For a complete network implementation, we achieved a peak performance of 1.3 GMACCs at 120 MHz frequency. Our implementation achieves a speed up of 4 times compared to software implementation on General Purpose Computer.

articleTitle: Optimal use of Inverse Distance Weighting method for temperature prediction
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: This article presents several ways of managing input data from different perspectives and the possibilities to use them on several interpolation methods and calibration techniques applied to a given data set. These techniques have been applied in order to obtain a better estimate of the temperature in a given geographical area. In order to determine the most accurate result, several analyses have been conducted on the identification of the temperature with the least deviation rate. As ways of measurement, several weather stations were first taken into consideration, whereupon this number increased exponentially, and eventually, calculations were made with the sole purpose of finding the minimum cumulative deviations from a certain point. By looking at the results, it follows that at least one of these data management methods, which constitutes a perspective in itself, can be used as a means to improve its appliance to methods of estimating linear weight, techniques and more. Moreover, in the technological era, an automatic selection for taking in reception the best value from the applied perspectives was developed and implemented. This selection offers a better disclosure for the most coherent information, template revealing and comparison to the latest results.

articleTitle: Loss Function Selection in NN based Classifiers: Try-outs with a Novel Method
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: Neural Network (NN) based classifiers are frequently used in different disciplines like pattern recognition, image classification, regression, etc. The optimized NNs are produced to achieve more robust classifiers in terms of preventing the fluctuations at error by yielding better convergence. However, in the literature, an extensive study is not available that examines one of the most important dynamics of NNs: loss function (error metric) of algorithm. In this study, ten different loss functions are evaluated to find out which one stays more coherent to utilize in NN based classifiers. For this purpose, a novel optimized classifier is handled using Gauss map based chaotic particle swarm optimization (GM-CPSO) with NN. GM-CPSO-NN classifiers including ten different loss functions are compared on two challenging tasks (Parkinson's disease recognition and epileptic seizure detection). Four metric based comparisons and 2-fold cross validation method are processed to objectively test the performance of classifiers. As a result, it's concluded that GM-CPSO-NN comprising mean square error (MSE) attains remarkable performance for both tasks, and MSE is revealed as the most appropriate error metric to be considered for the datasets including low or high pattern numbers.

Index Terms: Area Under Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve

articleTitle: A Full Study of the Conductivity of the Ionosphere for Iraq and Romania Regions
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: Free electrons and ions dominate the ionosphere. The ionosphere region could be defined from 80 to 1000 km. The largest free electrons and ions are concentrated approximately in the altitude 350 km for Iraq and Romania regions. The ionosphere has many characteristics like troposphere. The screening of the charges takes place in the troposphere. As a consequence, the ionosphere also suffers from discharging. In this work, it has been investigated that ionosphere is like the troposphere and they suffer from screening the charge and producing high voltage. The equations were used in this work, were derived for these purposes. The free electrons in the ionosphere made him a real perfect conductor cover the Earth. This conductor has variable conductivity extends from the equatorial region to the poles and has variable permittivity and permeability. As a consequence, this medium in the ionosphere will control the propagation of electromagnetic waves.

articleTitle: Evaluation of bearing assembly lifespan for electric motors - a case study on agriculture
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: In this work, the essential information on the bearing assemblies of electric drives is given. A problem of using bearing assemblies in agriculture conditions is also shown. In the paper, the wear rate of the working surface was chosen as the most critical parameter of the run-out process for the bearing assemblies. Dedicated tests were carried out to define the statistically substantiated values of this parameter. Values of gap clearance for bearing assemblies of electric motors have been specified that make it possible to evaluate the total expected lifespan of bearing assemblies for particular types of electric motors. The engineering method for evaluating the total and remaining lifespan of bearing assemblies of electric motors operated in agricultural production conditions has been developed. Values of the standard radial bearing clearance for various spindle heights have been determined that were calculated based on the standard values of gap clearance tolerance for mounting seats, and an example of calculations has been described. Values of an expected radial bearing clearance and those of lifespan of bearings for electric motor under control have been obtained, in the process of its operation, that characterize its wear rate, at a particular moment.

articleTitle: A Study on Applying Mobility Patterns for Multi-UAV Trajectory Planning
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: Trajectory planning tends to become one of the most important topics related to unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in the past years. The reasons for this include: hardware and software development, specific legislation that covers this topic, an increase interest from end-users or manufacturers and the list can continue. Scientific literature has unlimited information related to UAV influence on various fields, but limited on multi-UAV path planning, synchronization and cooperation. For this reason, the current paper has the objective to reveal a study on trajectory planning that will underline the importance of this topic in nowadays. A series of advantages and disadvantages will be covered throughout this paper to offer readers a clear perspective on applying mobility patterns for trajectory planning.

articleTitle: Simple Method to Increase Precision and Stability for Frequency Counters
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: There is well known that the high precision frequency counters register errors generated by equipment time-base, which are relevant especially on high frequency radio communication. Also, the modern equipment realizes mathematic functions in real-time mode, so as to ensure the user all necessary information. This kind of equipment is generally used in laboratory conditions, but also in real field for radio-application: broadcast radio transmitter, antenna and feeder calibration and other. Actual technology employs microcontrollers which ensures all functions, but in high frequency range this kind of application generates non-linear errors, which are unpredictable and difficult to compensate.The paper proposes a reasonable-cost method for solving the precision impediments for high frequency meter keeping the precision at the highest level possible.

articleTitle: Control System for Natural Gas Compression of Sinca Plant
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: The paper contains the authors' research on the automation of the Sinca gas compression installation, and it's structured in four parts. In the first part are analyzed bibliographic references regarding compressors and gas compression installations. The second part is dedicated to the study of the particularities of the Sinca gas compression installation. The third part contains modelling elements associated with the gas compressor. In this context, elements of mathematical modelling were developed and used in order to design an advanced compressor control structure. The simulation of the gas compression installation was performed using the Unisim Design simulator. In the current phase of research, the steady-state sensitivity analysis highlighted the feasibility of using the compressor power as the control agent of the automatic system.

articleTitle: Indoor positioning using Cell of Origin and LANDMARC approach
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: This paper presents a positioning system that is partially based on previous research papers and uses two widely known techniques in the specialized bibliography: Cell of Origin and LANDMARC. Comparations are made and characteristics are outlined between previous research papers, the above-mentioned techniques and other related work. The concept and implementation strategy are described along with the methodology used and the results obtained.

articleTitle: Factors that influence the change of human behavior in student's online activity
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: Today, people are living more and more changing times, they are subject of new challenges, they have to face new situations, for which they have prepared little or nothing. We refer here to education that has moved exclusively online, from one day to another, without training, without warnings, without tests. The students, like all teachers, in fact, were faced with a state of sin that at first they denied, rejected, negotiated, hated and, finally, accepted. This move to move courses exclusively online due to the COVID-19 pandemic has generated the rapid need for human change, a huge pressure to adapt and accept the unprecedented change in recent human history. As known, human behavior is strongly influenced by external and/or internal environmental factors, by their constancy or change. Thus, the change of the external environment generated a chain reaction of change of the internal environment, but also of the human behavior. This study aims to investigate how students' behavior has changed as a result of changing external factors and the influence of this change on their motivation.

articleTitle: Optimizing the Placement of Indoor Thermal Climate Sensors of an Iot Solution
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: In recent years, new and new IoT solutions are being developed, their growth rate being exponential, many of them dealing with sensor monitoring. Under these conditions, we need not only high-performance software solutions but also optimized and durable sensor systems. In this paper is presented a solution for positioning and mounting a sensor system used to monitor and perform calculations with indoor climate parameters. An independent sensor system is designed, completely detachable from the rest of the components of the IoT solution, for this being necessary the design and 3D printing of a box, the positioning of the sensors inside it and finally the 3D thermal analysis of the proposed solution.

articleTitle: Comparison of DotKernel and Symfony as PHP frameworks
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: This paper presents different PHP-based frameworks used for building robust, enterprise-level web applications. The paper focuses on the main features of the two frameworks, and then analyze some of the advantages and disadvantages of using each of them. DotKernel is a custom concept built by Apidemia, mainly used internally but present in the open-source environment. It is a collection of middleware applications built on top of the Zend Expressive microframework, implementing customized versions of some of the Zend Framework components. Symfony is also a concept consisting of a web application framework, a set of reusable, heavily used PHP components, and a community sharing a common philosophy.

articleTitle: Financial and technical forecast analysis of a cogeneration biomas plant - Case study in Romania
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: The production of electric and thermal energy using biomass is extremely important in the current context of the financial crisis and the continuous decrease of the reserves of conventional energy sources. This article analyzes the opportunity to locate the cogeneration plant that uses biomass from a rich region of Romania in this unconventional resource. Then the technical-economic indicators obtained by the plant during 6 years of operation are presented and analyzed. These indicators are used to develop a financial forecast extremely useful for the future development of the analyzed plant.

articleTitle: Automatic generation of quizzes for C programming language
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: In this paper we present a Java software application that illustrates the possibility to generate automatically quizzes for the C programming language. In many computer science faculties, C language is the first programming language to be studied, so, a good knowledge of this language will help a student learn better the other programming languages. The generated quiz will test a student's knowledge about the way of defining functions in C language. A random generated question is presented to the student and he will write his answer. The correctitude of the answer of the student is analysed using regular expressions.

articleTitle: Improving managerial skills for implementing innovations in education
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: Leadership is the art of mobilizing people, of inspiring them in the activity regarding the achievement of the expected objectives. Being a directed process, management is oriented towards achieving objectives by mobilizing human resources and ensuring organizational development, by promoting an educational strategy to increase human resources, focused on the formation and development of personality, able to make decisions independently. The main function of the management process is the decision, which represents a process of harmonization of objectives with human resources, which becomes the "engine of management", the "vital nerve", the "nodal point of management" and expresses the essence of management, the most representative product. of this activity. The entire activity of a leader is a permanent cycle of gathering information, analysis, decision making, control, etc. The efficiency of the decision depends on the professional competence of the manager, on the capacity to mobilize and guide the team of the educational institution, on ensuring the maximum capitalization of the human and material potential, in order to respond to all requirements and actions of educational factors. This paper aims to present and analyze the conditions that must be met by education managers to develop skills in implementing educational innovations.

articleTitle: Mechanical ventilation device with adapted parameters to assist patients infected with the SARS-CoV-2 virus
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: Patients in the intensive care unit (ICU), dependent on mechanical ventilation, need the best care, from hospitalization to discharge and even later. Different tools are needed in different stages of therapy. The variability and diversity of therapy tools clearly improve decisions in clinical practice as well as treatments. This article presents the design of a device for mechanical ventilation of patients in intensive care units. The ventilator presented will be intended for use on patients requiring sedation and intubation, ensuring mechanical ventilation and monitoring of vital functions of patients.

articleTitle: A multiple choice OMP algorithm for DOA estimation
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: This study describes an algorithm which improves the direction of arrival (DOA) estimation of electromagnetic waves to a uniform, linear array (ULA) of antennas. Under some conditions, referring to the low number of sources, the algorithm allows obtaining an angle resolution better than that bounded by the limited number of antennas. It can be obtained by reducing the topic to one of solving a set of equations, with a sparse solution.

articleTitle: A software platform for monitoring radiation detection systems
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: In order to permanently monitor the environmental radiation which could result in radiological hazards but also to improve accuracy of scientific results regarding cosmic particles, new systems are being developed. However, from various causes these systems are prone to errors and false alarms can be triggered thus any change in the operating parameters of the radiation detection systems has to be detected immediately. The main objective of this paper is to provide a universal solution for automatic monitoring of radiation detection systems. The proposed software solution fulfills the high-level objectives of this paper – the implementation of a software solution which automatically monitors a radiation detection system. The solution was developed and works for a specific system, but it can be used for other detection systems as well with minor changes such as definition of the class attributes.

articleTitle: Reliability analysis for laboratory development of a traffic light controller
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: Traffic light controllers are widely used in road infrastructure equipment. From the basic function, of controlling the traffic lights, their applications have widely extended to incorporate information from vehicle detectors, vehicles, and communications with its "neighbours" or a central control point. But in all the implementations, the two most critical factors in their operation remains safety and reliability. As they should operate continuously and guarantee clear and correct indications on traffic lights, even in malfunctioning situations, their design must incorporate extensive fail-safe functions that could properly manage all the possible faults. In this paper the authors are proposing hardware solutions to increase the reliability of a traffic light controller. These were testing for validity in computer simulations.

articleTitle: Fast Method for Detecting Geographical Center of Romania using AutoCAD
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: This paper explains in detail a novel step-by-step method for fast computation of the geographical center of a bordered region, using Google Earth, GIMP and AutoCAD. The novelty of the paper consists in how the three well-known software applications were combined to calculate the geographical center of a country. The most important step was how GIMP was used for translating the map from Google Earth to AutoCAD. An estimation of the accuracy of this method is also presented. A discussion on ways to increase the accuracy also appears in the paper. The country used throughout the paper for testing the method was Romania. The algorithm identified the geographical center of Romania in the vicinity of Făgăraş train station, South of the city of Făgăraş, in Brasov county of Romania.

articleTitle: Optimize Recommendation Engine for Marketing System in Healthcare CRM
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: Healthcare marketing is one of the most interesting research domains due to the high complexity and legal regulations of the medical data on the one side and the large volume of data required by marketing processes on the other side. Current research proposes a solution of adapting a commonly used marketing process, recommendation to healthcare industry needs to healthcare industry. Optimization of the standard recommendation processes have been identified as the main point of adaptation due to the high volume of data available in healthcare systems along with the need of analyzing the complete set of available data. Caching results represents one of the most common optimization techniques used in software implementation and due to highly sensitivity of medical data appears to be non-applicable. This paper is making use of segmentation of data sets combining patient profiles in target groups that are to be passed to recommendation scenarios as input data allowing catching results for healthcare recommendation scenarios.

articleTitle: Internet Hate speech – case study of Poland, Romania, India and Bulgaria
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: As online hate is ubiquitous and spread on the cyberspace, new studies are needed to understand its nature and evolution. We have researched young adults from Poland, India, Romania and Bulgaria to study their hate experiences. We have found out that online hate is an inherent part of their cyberspace activities. This implies a necessity of ongoing education at this field as current skills of participants on dealing with hate speech and possibilities of support as well as legal responsibilities remain relatively low.

articleTitle: Continuing Education - Alternative for Capitalizing of the Professional Development Needs of Teachers
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: This paper represents a psycho-pedagogical study on the need for teacher training, in terms of professional development of teachers. At the same time, the paper presents the idea of the concept of mixed continuous training is the transition from a continuous training focused on "the same approaches for all" - regardless of students' skills, professional interests or personal life pressures - to self-motivating continuous training, in agreement with the individual needs of professional development, therefore self-determining both in terms of individual goals and in terms of praxeology. In this context, the evolution of science and the multidimensionality of contemporary life (which can sometimes generate existential complications) become sources of adaptation and to meet the implicit needs, by capitalizing on multimedia technologies and by expanding the possibilities of communication. What seems difficult turns into an advantage, given that the continuous training of teachers brings the innovations articulated to the contemporary world.

articleTitle: Sensitivity Analysis Based on the Defined Load Threshold for a new Fuel Economy Strategy used in Fuel Cell Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: In this paper, a new fuel economy strategy for fuel cell vehicles is proposed. Its performance is analyzed using the sensitivity analysis of the load threshold, and indicators such as fuel economy and oxygen excess ratio. The fuel economy strategy uses fuel and air flows in a switched manner to operate the fuel cell system efficiently. The obtained fuel economy is highlighted compared to the reference strategy based on static feed-forward control.

articleTitle: Analyze of Eco-financial Impact of PV System Integration in Educational Institutions. Case Study in Romania
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: Educational institutions represent both a significant share of the total public institutions in a country such as 45.93% in Romania and important consumers of electricity. The model of electricity consumption of a pre-university educational institution can be extended to the vast majority of these institutions. That is why the integration of a photovoltaic system that generates electricity for such a consumer can become a very useful reference. The article proposes the integration of a PV system in a known location. Its operation simulation is done using the BlueSol Design programming environment and the analysis of the economic and environmental impact on the entire lifetime of the PV system uses the Open LCA software application. The results obtained may be interesting initial data for other studies on this topic.

articleTitle: Analysis of blood by Spectroscopy Near Infrared
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: Measuring blood elements in a non-invasive manner is an important step for biomedicine and for finding health information in a timely manner for patients. In this article we discuss methods about measurement of formed elements blood by non-invasive near infrared: erytrocytes, leukocytes and platelets.

articleTitle: AC home appliances retrofiting for DC microgrids
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: This work demonstrates the possibility of retrofitting the AC home appliances for direct usage in DC microgrids using simple and low-cost methods. Nowadays, most of the appliances are using AC-DC conversion, which creates the possibility of direct connection of home appliances to DC voltage grids. The paper shows the practical results made on an air conditioning/heat pump system, an induction heating cooker and a refrigerator by retrofitting to a 350V DC grid.

articleTitle: Use of OPC Protocol, DeltaV Distributed System and Simulink for Level Control with PI and IMC Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: The paper study the possibility of using the OPC protocol to transmit data in real time between DeltaV distributed system and Simulink environment in order to develop a level control system in a real plant. The DeltaV system is configured in order to acquire the level value from the transducer, and to transmit the commands for the control valve and the pump. The control algorithms, Proportional-Integral (PI) and Internal Model Control (IMC), are implemented in Simulink. In order to facilitate the real time connection between DeltaV and Simulink, OPC protocol functions are used. The developed level control system is studied for changes of set-point and disturbance. The results obtained for the two cases (PI and IMC algorithms) are compared in terms of transient time, time delay and overshoot. All the results are obtained for the real plant.

articleTitle: An Investigation on Twelve Sectors Direct Torque Control for Induction Motors fed by Matrix Converter
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: Direct torque control for the induction motor fed matrix converter (DTC-MC) has been extensively studied. The control of the stator flux and the torque in DTC-MC is made through voltage vector selection in the switching table with 6 sectors. This switching table has some voltage vectors that do not produce the strongest torque response.This paper considers DTC-MC using a switching table with 12 sectors (12-DTC-MC structure), which provide a better torque response than DTC-MC using a switching table with 6 sectors (6-DTC-MC structure). The advantages and disadvantages of both structures are analyzed through the simulation results.

articleTitle: Development and Testing of Approach for Separated Training of Branches of Multi-Task Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: This paper explores the possibility of building a new model on the basis of an already trained neural network to perform an extended number of tasks, using the knowledge available in the original model. Possible areas of application are determined, the influence of such an approach on the accuracy and speed of the obtained multi-task model is investigated in comparison with a set of single-task models each of which fulfills specific task.

articleTitle: Improved Classification Accuracy of Four Class FNIRS-BCI
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: Experimentation and analysis in brain-computer interface (BCI) has increasingly been receiving quite some consideration as a substitute communication possibility for patients who are severely paralyzed in the last few years. To measure brain activities using optical signals a fairly new and non-invasive brain imaging tool can be put to test know as Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS). Comparability low cost, safety, portability and wear ability are some of the main advantages of imaging of brain using this non-invasive modality. We propose in this paper to apply this relatively new non-invasive fNIRS technique to make an image of brain activities during four different mental tasks. These tasks include Mental Arithmetic (MA), Motor Imagery (i.e. Left-Hand and Right-Hand Motor Imagery) and Rest. fNIRS data used is an open access dataset which was collected by Continuous-wave imaging system (NIR Scout NIRx GmbH, Berlin, Germany) with the sampling frequency of 10 Hz. The research we have done in this paper Data synchronization is performed before the data is preprocessed. After the preprocessing and signal analysis of data our results shows hemodynamic behavior of multiple patterns during the tasks performed. These unique patterns of hemodynamic behavior can be used to differentiate and distinguish different task. We were able to compare, differentiate and distinguish the brain signal activities captured while performing 4 different tasks using 3 different classifiers i.e. Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA), Support Vector Machine (SVM) and K Nearest Neighbor (KNN). The average classification accuracy of above 90% is achieved by using K Nearest Neighbors (KNN).

articleTitle: Towards the development of a personalized healthcare solution for elderly: from user needs to system specifications
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: Due to the demographic changes, the demand for care services adapted to the elderly will have an unprecedented growth globally. In this situation, maintaining quality of life (QoL) and wellbeing for older adults will need support of complementary, nontraditional, ICT-based care practices. vINCI project, part of the European research effort in this domain, aims to deliver an integrated technology for the monitoring and instrumentation of the QoL intervention for older adults. The process of designing the vINCI application is based on the patient profile model that will be the input to provide personalized healthcare. The profile is used as evidence to evaluate the impact of vINCI solution on the perceived quality of life provided by caregivers. This paper proposes a complementary approach in modelling the user profile by identifying the needs and preferences of elderly and translating them into development requirements of the vINCI monitoring platform. In this respect, this paper proposes a methodology and methods to define user needs, which are based upon the User Centered Design principles, such as user surveys. The needs survey provides information that is used to specify the needed functional and nonfunctional requirements that vINCI platform must support.

articleTitle: Energy management strategies for hybrid electric vehicles - vosviwer bibliometric analysis
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: The electric vehicle is one of the best solutions in the fight against pollution, but they need certain energy management strategies to improve their features. The purpose of our research is to identify, trough different types of bibliographic maps (maps based on network data, maps based on bibliographic data or maps based on text data), the optimal energy management strategy that could be used on electric vehicles.The essential element among this paper are the energy management strategies that we selected from articles identified in the database of Web of Science and, with VOSviewer, we build bibliometric analysis from various perspectives. We have made the analyze on strategies like reducing emissions, fuel economy, performance, etc. and we can observe that there are appearing different strategies that are using combinations, positions and algorithms for the component elements. There for, the energy management strategies are taking care to put in the balance all the important elements. In the results, we can see that one of the most used elements are the fuel cell, supercapacitor, the battery, the algorithm that we use and the control strategies that we choose.We have exported various maps, based on the next subjects: the occurrence of the topics and the strengths of his connections and geographic distribution and made a classification of the strategies that can be used to improve different factors.

articleTitle: Stock Market Prediction Using a Deep Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: The objective of this research is to develop a Deep Learning model to forecast the stock price market, by using the variant of Long Short-Term Memory (Deep LSTM). This model predicts close price of the stock for the next day, choosing as inputs the following data: open, high, low, adj close and close prices. We have used the historical stock prices data from yahoo's financial website over 10 years, by choosing two index datasets: Dow Jones Industrial (DJI) and S and P 500 index (daily values). We designed the architectural structure of the deep learning model using eleven LSTM layers and choosing ADAM optimization tools. In order to get effective in the forecasting model, we have tested the network with different iterations and epochs. We have estimated the effectiveness of our proposed model by using the following performance indicators: the mean square error (MSE), the root mean square error (RMSE), the mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) and the accuracy of model. The experimental results clearly show that our Deep LSTM model has the highest accuracy values when comparing with other related researches. Hence, we can conclude that our Deep LSTM model is suitable for accurate prediction of the stock market time series.

articleTitle: Cybersecurity Perspectives for Smart Building Automation Systems
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: As the built environment becomes the hallmark of urbanisation tendencies worldwide, people have come to rely on buildings for a large majority of their daily activities. Modern buildings are equipped with new sensor technologies and advanced controllers, integrated through communication interfaces and application software to handle various required functions through automation. This is partially extended to legacy buildings through retrofitting. Integration of these new technologies opens up the automation system of the building to internal and external attackers. The challenges related to cybersecurity identified are partially similar to the industrial control system domain while adding specific constraints for the built environment as compared to a production/manufacturing environment, which relate to human safety, security and privacy aspects. We provide a critical overview of cybersecurity challenges for smart building automation systems by focusing on key areas of development at the device, system and communication and interoperability levels. A representative example for BACnet protocol features and tools is provided.

articleTitle: Data Security in Smart Grid
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: Looking at the Smart Grid as a Cyber - Physical system of great complexity, the paper synthesizes the main IT security issues that may arise. Security issues are seen from a hybrid point of view, combining theory of information with system theory. Smart Grid has changed dramatically over the past years. With modern technologies, such as Big Data or Internet of Things (IoT), the Smart Grid is evolving into a more interconnected and dynamic power network model.

articleTitle: A practical implementation of modern Distributed Control Systems in Electric Power Substations
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: This paper presents a practical implementation of a modern DCS in energy sector, applicable for electric power transmission and distributions substations. When dealing with aging infrastructure the reward from investing in modern automation solution can be substantial, with benefits such increasing productivity, cost savings, safety operations, scalable solution and a better integration in the modern IT facilities. The modern DCS systems evolved into a flexible and scalable automation solutions, which make them mandatory in the actual competitive energy business environment. Comparing to PLCs and traditional DCS, the modern DCS systems are designed to provide automation solution in a safe, reliable and cost-effectively manner. The main goal of this article is to present and suggest an optimal DCS design and functional solutions taking into consideration customer requirements, international and customer applicable norms, budget constraint, hardware and software limitations, integration of existing equipment, cybersecurity and low impact of the monitored and controlled process for extension and future growth. The principles presented in this paper can be found implemented in Romania mainly in the electric power transmission substations, owned by Romanian Transmission and System Operator CNTEE Transelectrica SA.

articleTitle: The Current Trends of Virtual Reality Applications in Medical Education
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: The study of human computer interaction in using immersive technologies has become very essential and critical. Immersive technologies have been used significantly in medical education. In the medical field, real-life training is not always possible. The main reasons are cost and safety. Thus, alternatives in providing and achieving a better educational medical training platform are needed. There is a growing interest in using virtual reality (VR) for training and learning in the medical field. The use of virtual reality in educational training may facilitate a successful medical learning process without involving a real human. The technology allows learners to adapt different learning styles in ways that are not suited to traditional teaching. This study aims to investigate efforts and opportunities for using VR technologies for medical training purposes. This paper identifies and summarizes VR tools used for surgical training especially in laparoscopic surgery, arthroscopy and orthopedic surgery. We also present the advantages of medical training using VR.

articleTitle: A Biometric Identification System with Kernel SVM and Feature-level Fusion
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: The paper presents a biometric system with optimization for identification. The design combines 2 biometrics (fingerprint and palmprint) with feature-level functional fusion, avoiding the concatenation. Data classification is done with a kernel SVM (Support Vector Machine) model and a multi-class extension. The experimental achievements show that the performance improvements are provided by the feature-level fusion together with an optimized design of the biometric data classifier. The model can be applied in use-cases in which the identity of the individuals should be guessed only based on the biometric credential.

articleTitle: Taking advantage of unsupervised learning in incident response
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: This paper looks at new ways to improve the necessary time for incident response triage operations. By employing unsupervised K-means, enhanced by both manual and automated feature extraction techniques, the incident response team can quickly and decisively extrapolate malicious web requests that concluded to the investigated exploitation. More precisely, we evaluated the benefits of different visualization enhancing methods that can improve feature selection and other dimensionality reduction techniques. Furthermore, early tests of the gross framework have shown that the necessary time for triage is diminished, more so if a hybrid multi-model is employed. Our case study revolved around the need for unsupervised classification of unknown web access logs. However, the demonstrated principals may be considered for other applications of machine learning in the cybersecurity domain.

articleTitle: Neural road semantic segmentation in driving scenarios
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to review the best semantic segmentation algorithms which involve deep neural networks and to compare one of the most used ones on a specific task for autonomous driving - road segmentation, regarding the accuracy and the time. We analyze the state of the art, then we propose a new dataset for road semantic segmentation consisting of images from our university campus, annotated by our team and taking into account the time of the day. We analyze the results of the road segmentation task obtained from the best segmentation models and we describe some metrics (accuracy, IoU) regarding the time of the day (day, dusk, night).

articleTitle: Merging Operations Technology with Information Technology
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: Control systems have evolved extensively in the last century. Longer product lifecycles and the discrepancy between operations technology and information technology represent a challenge in today's innovation sector. Starting from a vague, surreal idea of autonomy to the development of the first systems operated by artificial intelligence algorithms, the concept of automated self-managing systems has had significant implications in the field of information technology and operations technology. This paper contributes to the acceleration of the decisional process of merging operations technology with information technology. The purpose is to expose the benefits through studies, examples, and explain the current levels of automation and the evolution from data ingestion, connectivity, communication, processing to decision-making practices supported by artificial intelligence.

articleTitle: Experimental, ad hoc, online, inter-university student e-contest during the pandemic – Lessons learned
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: Purpose: We analyze the effect of the current pandemic on students e-contests. Method: We compare the e-contest with the 10 previous editions of the same but face-to-face contest. Statistical and NLP analysis are applied. Conclusions: Apparently the competition did not suffer because of being a virtual one; the basic interconnectivity means arise no serious technical issue. Disadvantages found: the interconnectivity is more limited than for the face-to-face case; online jury-competitors interactivity is poorer than face-to-face interactivity; human factors, higher uncertainties in the organization process, and less time to spend in the process for the local organizers are major limiting factors; concerns on the participation and evaluation fairness are higher; involuntary gender discrimination seems lower, but persists; there are serious concerns related to privacy, including differential privacy; peculiarities of the presented topics and of the evaluation process emerged, but it is unclear if they are related to the online nature of the competition, to the extra stress on the participants during the pandemic, to other factors, or are random. Some conclusions may be valid for the analyzed case only, yet some are general enough for being worth reporting. A preprint was published in ArXiv.

articleTitle: Credit Scoring Using Deep Learning Driven by Optimization Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: Credit scoring as good or bad has a significant importance for financial institutions. This paper presents a Deep Learning approach for credit scoring. We have defined the credit score as a cost obtained by a weighted sum of the number of false negative errors (FN) and the number of false positive errors (FP). Our objective was to obtain the lowest possible score. The largest weight is allocated to the indicator FN (this corresponds to the prediction of bad credit as good credit). As a consequence, our best credit score corresponds to minimization of Miss Alarm Rate (MAR) for a given sum of total errors. The proposed model of cost minimization uses state of the art mathematical algorithms and deep learning techniques. In our work, we use optimization algorithms for selecting a deep learning neural network architecture and for finding the optimum hyperparameters. The method is tested using the German credit dataset. The best result leads to a MAR of 3%.

articleTitle: Visualization in Medical System Interfaces: UX Guidelines
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: Visualization is an important element in user experience (UX). Thus, it should be considered in designing an interface of a system. Visualization can help users to accomplish their duties in an intuitive manner. This is essential especially in the medical field. To the best of our knowledge none of existing UX guidelines, for designing an interface have included visualization factor. The aim of this study is to propose a set of UX guidelines that include visualization elements for designing an interface of a medical system. This paper presents a survey on visualization elements that contribute to UX and proposes a nine UX guidelines for building interfaces of medical systems. The proposed guidelines consist of visualizations elements including graphs, symbols, icons, shapes, pictographic, infographic, pattern, layout, colors, and terminologies used.

articleTitle: On Change Detection in the Complexity of Time Series
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: This work is an exploratory and preliminary study on change detection in the structure of time series based on structural entropy processing, with direct application to fault detection in production processes. Starting with some theoretical elements related to entropy, various types of estimators are presented, and some are discussed, as the approximate entropy (ApEn), the sample entropy (SampEn), and the multiscale entropies (MSE). The case studies contain synthetized signals as white Gaussian noise, 1/f noise, and random signals with a probabilistic structure, ended with real vibration signals generated by faults in bearings. Finally, a change detection criterion is promoted based on the average of multiscale entropy and cumulative sum technique. The study is useful for a better understanding of the entropy-based methods for change detection in the structure of the time-series and it prepares the next level of the research, i.e. methods based on Renyi entropy with recursive estimators – when possible - and their extension to chaotic and stochastic systems, especially from the structure change detection point of view.

articleTitle: Performance of cloudlets in task implementation using ant colony optimization technique
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: In general the term fog computing is aimed towards minimization of network congestion and process the data by inheriting as well as applying knowledge. In addition to that it can also facilitate to different data sources linked with sensors as well as actuators. The basic terminologies like cloudlets which are linked with fog computing have the provision of quite similar services as with cloud computing. But in many cases these are associated with large number of resources. Considering its computing capabilities, each component linked with the system has the significance to locally process the data. But sometimes it is required to process the heterogeneous data from multiple sources implementing the available resources in cloud. In many situations, there is a provision of extension of computing resources in cloud with similar as well as dissimilar data along with storage allocation. In such situation, the systems linked with fog computing are quite competent towards processing the data and the platforms will be quite appropriate towards location sensitive applications. The intensification of the applications is measured along with security mechanisms and will impact on the issues with feasible solutions. Also while facilitating the computing in cloud, the security measures cannot be reflected directly towards computation. Particularly it is responsible towards managing as well as enhancing the performance of systems associated with virtual platforms along with virtual clusters. As comparing with the cloud computing, the cloudlets perform better with enhanced security. In this case it is being proposed to focus on linkages of databases with them. Also it is being aimed to analyze the task implementation using ant colony optimization technique prioritizing the operational linkage of databases as well as scheduling mechanisms of tasks in the cloudlets within the virtual machines.

articleTitle: Implementation of MediCare Social Media System
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: Smart technologies such as computers, smartphones, smart bracelets, smart medical devices can be used by medicinal organizations because of their enhanced usability, multiple uses, low costing, flexibility, mobility, reliability, and new capabilities. This encouraged health organizations to boost their demand for new healthcare technologies and enable users to multiple access medical services and improve the user experience. The current paper presents the implementation of an integrated system - MediCare system, which has the role of a medical social media system. To improve the health services in Iraq, we developed the MediCare system to take advantage of techniques like social-oriented networks, smartphone, wearable devices, medical devices. The MediCare system can be used on tablets and smartphones operating on the Android system through its Android App Interface. In addition, the MediCare web application can be used by devices like computers, smartphones, and tablets.

articleTitle: The impact of the virtual learning environment in managing the knowledge transmitted to students
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: This research follows the evolution, role and interactions between e-learning and specific social/educational activities, under crisis conditions too. The impossibility of the physical presence of teachers and students in educational institutions has automatically led to the use of online platforms. Taking account of the changes in learning activities in the context of the effects of the pandemic facing all mankind, we wanted to highlight the current state of research in the Web of Science for keywords "e-learning and University".

articleTitle: Target Audience Response Analysis in Out-of-home Advertising Using Computer Vision
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: In this paper we aim to analyze the response of the target audience to out-of-home advertising panels mounted in display windows. We track people passing in front of the panels and, if they approach the panel, looking directly at it, we analyze their facial movements, to see whether the advert appeals to them or not. The approach is based on video data gathering using a static IP camera, storage and analysis, aiming to deliver real-time results. We use neural networks and support vector machines to determine facial microexpression. Results are correlated with information about the adverts displayed to be of use to advertising providers.

articleTitle: Technological and ethical aspects of autonomous driving in a multicultural society
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: At the beginning of a new decade, major car manufacturers are heading towards the finish line of the autonomous driving race. Whereby advanced driver assisted systems and electric mobility are already implemented and gaining an ever-increasing market share, autonomous cars are mostly still in the testing and development phase. Are humans ready for full autonomy on the road, or will the society resist the data-driven artificial intelligence approach of driving? This paper contributes to the acceleration of autonomous driving innovation and understanding of the underlying concepts. It will expose, explain, and uncover most technological and ethical aspects around autonomous, driverless cars considering compliance and regulatory affairs, which are inevitably impacting today's and tomorrow's society.

articleTitle: Modeling the Total Electron Content variation in the Ionosphere for Improved Positional Accuracy
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: The total electron content (TEC) in the ionosphere produces a group delay in the propagating signal of a navigational satellite and produces a range error. This error in Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) is corrected by the fixed Klobuchar ionospheric model in the single-frequency receivers. The performance of the Klobuchar error correction is lowered due to the irregular and complex distribution of TEC in the equatorial and low latitude regions. This is further affected in the equinox month of March and during geomagnetic disturbances. In this paper, model using the Support Vector Machine (SVM) is proposed to predict the ionospheric TEC range half an hour in advance. The TEC thus predicted can be further used for estimating a suitable correction to minimize the range error. The model can apriori estimate the range of mean value of TEC at t+δt using the input features at time t. The model is trained using the TEC values of all days, Disturbed Storm Index (Dst), Auroral Electrojet index (AE), time of the day and extracted features of TEC. The performance of the model is also compared by changing the input features and its accuracy is measured using precision, recall, F score and the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve. It is observed that the model performance is improved by adding extracted features of TEC and is able to predict the mean TEC range half an hour in advance with better accuracy. The model is also tested with unseen storm day TEC data and is found to perform well with 80% accuracy. The equatorial anomaly region near the geomagnetic equator is chosen for the study. The TEC data is obtained from the International GNSS Service (IGS) dual-frequency receiver located at IISC, Bengaluru, India for the equinox month of the year 2015 for training the model.

articleTitle: Internet of Things Traffic Characterization using flow and packet analysis
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: The "Internet of Things" (IoT) era is becoming a reality and the number of smart objects or devices connected to the Internet is rapidly increasing every year. Nevertheless, most IoT devices are known to be built with limited resources (CPU, memory, battery life etc.), thus not every security mechanism can be included in their development process. Given these properties of IoT devices, it became imperative for researchers and specialists in the information security field to understand how "normal" IoT traffic profile looks like to create a baseline for IoT environments behavior and define what characteristics can further be used as indicators for prevention and detection of cyber-attacks. In this paper, we proposed a methodology for distinguishing normal or legitimate traffic from abnormal or malicious traffic and identifying specific IoT environments network traffic characteristics from our analysis. This work is based on two existing public datasets that were examined in order to perform the analysis.

articleTitle: Acquiring businesss intelligence through data science: A practical approach
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: Throughout the history of humanity, the way that humans transmit intelligence from generation to generation has changed multiple times. Beginning verbally and through manuscripts, continuing with patented inventions, official and private documents, nowadays, the different ways of adapting and implementing the knowledge acquired through data are being highlighted. Whether with regards to human, artificial, or mixed intelligence, data can provide consistent and meaningful answers to address the challenges of today's businesses. This scientific paper contributes to the vision of a hybrid human and artificial intelligence approach, thus explaining, exemplifying, and presenting research on how today's organizations apply the concept of data efficiency and effectiveness from a business intelligence perspective. The fact that decision-makers can be more performant with the help of data science and machine learning has the power of unlocking strengths and opportunities at an unprecedented rate and therefor is the new norm in the modern business world.

articleTitle: Different working conditions identification of a PV power plant using hierarchical clustering
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: This article presents big data analysis, based on the measurements from a stationary power quality (PQ) monitoring system of a 15 kW PV power plant. The study period is one year - 2018. In the article, a unified PQ database was proposed, which consists of PQ parameters and active power level. Then cluster analysis (CA) was performed to indicate the different working conditions of a PV power plant. The Ward algorithm was selected to obtain the automatic classification due to the data features. The importance rate of parameters for each classification was calculated, to indicate which parameters were important in point of different clusters obtained. Additionally, the PQ level comparison between the clusters was realized to assess the indicated working conditions of a PV power plant.

articleTitle: Smart Integrative System for the Battery Balance Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: In recent years, the electric vehicle industry and industrial electricity storage facilities have expanded. However, even if the type of batteries used is generally the same (Li-Ion 18650 battery type), the management systems of these batteries are specially designed for each application. This phenomenon leads to an increase of installations' costs and, most of the times, the system design starts from the scratch. This work starts from the need to develop a modular system, easily to be built and maintained, thus designing a complete smart system for monitoring all the component cells of the battery in electric vehicles, electric recreational vehicles or industrial installations. In order to carry out this project, several monitoring alternatives presented in the literature have been considered and a system consisting of 4 individual modules was developed: two modules with different precisions for monitoring the voltages of the component cells of the battery, a module for monitoring the charging or discharging current and a main module that interacts with the user and coordinates the all other modules.

articleTitle: Wilt Dataset-based Comparative Analysis of Three Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: This paper carries out a comparative analysis of three neural networks and their specific kernel machine learning algorithms, namely Inverse Weighted K-means in Online mode (IWKO1), evolving Fuzzy Optimally Pruned Extreme Learning Machine (eF-OP-ELM) and Support Vector Machine (SVM). The presentation of IWKO1, eF-OP-ELM and SVM is given and associated with their mathematical background, and the steps of their implementations are next outlined. The comparative analysis involves two performance indices, prediction accuracy and execution time, measured after the implementation on the Wilt dataset. The analysis is important in the context of the need to handle big data volumes in terms of using special algorithms, which are specially designed to process appropriately such data and information.

Author Keywords: evolving Fuzzy Optimally Pruned Extreme Learning Machines
Inverse Weighted K-means in Online mode

articleTitle: ROetry: First Steps Towards Computer Generated Poetry in Romanian Language
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: Over the past decades, the scientists in the field of technology dreamt of a utopia in which computers are human-like machines, capable of comprehending emotions and feelings. Poetry, the sign of culture and intelligence, could be the final test to determine if computers are capable of expressing themselves. Can a computer write poetry? This is the question whose answer could make art and science, the two spheres of knowledge that have seemed to always exclude each other, finally meet.This paper approaches the state of automatic poetry generation by studying the current achievements and the methodologies developed so far for this purpose. We propose a Romanian-based application developed by using both Markov chain and LSTM recurrent neural network models. The goal is to generate a text with metrical constraints (rhyme, number of syllables), that can be read as poetry.

articleTitle: A survey about industries that blockchain can transform
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: Blockchain become, because of its security, decentralized architecture and flexibility, one of the most important technologies in our days. Blockchain is a very good alternative for traditional system architectures. Researchers in almost all domains tried to adapt this new technology in their area and develop new solutions. The blockchain community has grown significantly and the proposed solutions become more and more complex. Problems like fraud, data integrity and data manipulation, distributed authority, information privacy and security are solved through blockchain. The technology can be successfully combined with traditional centralized architectures creating in this way hybrid systems with high complexity and security. The propose of the current paper is to make a review over multiple domains of solutions developed using blockchain, to compare their architectures, and to emphasize the initial requirements and constrains and how this technology was applied.

articleTitle: A Survey on Decision Support Systems in Water Management
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: Water is one of the most important resources for survival and it is extremely necessary to make good decisions regarding its management. The technology has advanced and offers us Decision Support Systems (DSS), using complex solutions. In recent decades, the number of DSSs developed for water resource management has grown significantly, and computer systems have become more complex by integrating water management processes, Internet of things (IoT) sensors, multi-criteria decisions and why not even serious games. The involvement of several stakeholders in the decision-making process has high importance for a successful DSS, facilitating the analysis of approaches from different fields. In order to find a cost-efficient balance in managing water resources, it is necessary to reach several objectives in different fields. The current paper aims to make a brief review of technological development and integration to highlight the socio-economic benefits.

articleTitle: Smart Battery Monitoring System Software Design
publicationTitle: 2020 12th International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: This paper presents the software design for a smart integrative system developed to monitor the balance of batteries, system designed and realized in the work [1]. The following software applications have been developed: the software of the voltage measurement modules, the software for the currents' measurement and the software of the central unit. There are also presented the user interaction with the central unit, some experimental results and the Battery Management System (BMS) testing on an electric scooter.
